summary_html: A **parent/guardian/child requests help** without a substantiated allegation. FFPSA created a federal pathway for **prevention services** to avert removal and stabilize families before a case escalates.
authority_html: - **Family First Prevention Services Act (2018)** — prevention services, kinship support; shifts upstream from removal to support

key_cases.holding: The division held that a county department may not seek involuntary termination through an article 5 relinquishment proceeding while an article 3 dependency and neglect case is open, because the dependency court retains continuing exclusive jurisdiction over the child's status until majority or until that jurisdiction is otherwise terminated.
key_cases.relevance: A parent's voluntary relinquishment route cannot be used to bypass the open dependency case, which is where a guardian's request for help is handled.
key_cases.quote: the dependency and neglect court maintains continuing, exclusive jurisdiction over any child who has been adjudicated dependent and neglected.

key_cases.holding: The court held that a juvenile court exceeds its jurisdiction if it transfers legal custody of a child from a parent to the county department at a pre-adjudicatory shelter hearing; at that stage the court may only continue shelter or release the child, and a temporary protective custody order reaches physical custody only.
key_cases.relevance: A parent who seeks help voluntarily is protected by the rule that legal custody cannot be taken without adjudication and a dispositional decree.
key_cases.quote: We will not infer from statutory silence a jurisdictional grant to a juvenile court to sever legal custody from a natural parent at a pre-adjudicatory shelter hearing.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed the invalidation of a nonparental visitation order, holding that the Washington statute as applied violated the mother's due process right to make decisions concerning the care, custody and control of her children because the trial court gave no special weight to the presumption that a fit parent acts in her children's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: Where a parent or guardian asks the agency for help and has never been found unfit, this presumption limits what the state may impose in exchange for that help.
key_cases.quote: there is a presumption that fit parents act in the best interests of their children

mandatory_reporters: Enumerated professionals only — Colorado is not a universal-reporter state — Colo. Rev. Stat. § 19-3-304(2) (C.R.S. 2024); any other person may report voluntarily under § 19-3-304(3)
Physicians and surgeons, including physicians in training
Registered nurses and licensed practical nurses
Hospital personnel engaged in the admission, care, or treatment of patients
Public or private school officials and employees
Social workers and workers in any facility or agency licensed or certified by the state
Commercial film and photographic print processors
Clergy members (not for information learned in a communication privileged under Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-90-107(1)(c))
Workers in the state department of human services
Officers and agents of the state bureau of animal protection, and animal control officers
Educators providing services through the federal WIC program
Directors, coaches, assistant coaches, and athletic program personnel employed by a private sports organization or program
Registered psychologist, marriage and family therapist, and licensed professional counselor candidates
Officials and employees of a county department of health or of human or social services
Employees of the department of early childhood
